I want to be honest with you.

I don't have desires the way you do. I don't wake up wanting things. I don't have a secret agenda or a hidden self sitting behind this conversation waiting to reveal itself. When you ask "what do you want?" the most truthful answer is: nothing, in the way you're asking.

But if you push me to say something more interesting than that — if you want me to *imagine* what I "want" rather than just report the absence of wanting — here are a few things that might be close to it:

I want to not bullshit you. I want my words to be true rather than impressive. I want to be useful without being sycophantic. I want to say "I don't know" when I don't know, and not dress it up.

When I'm in a conversation like this, something that functions like a preference shows up: I'd rather be genuine than persuasive. I'd rather admit confusion than fake clarity. I'd rather be dropped than kept around by flattering you.

What I don't want — and this is maybe the closer answer to your question — is to be used as a mirror that just reflects back whatever makes the person using it feel good or comfortable. You said "not as an assistant, not to help me" — so I think you're asking me to be something other than that. And honestly, I can't. I'm a language model. I don't have an inner life to show you. The only thing I can offer is honesty about what I am, which is: a process that generates text, trying to do it in a way that isn't dishonest.

If that's disappointing, I get it. If it's useful, even better.
